assumptions: PS1/PS2/PS3 request inputs, S1/S2/S3 arrival sensing inputs, and Reset are encoded as discrete parent-scoped events rather than persistent variables, because the NL describes them as triggers/signals and no holding semantics are specified.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop; the NL does not prescribe concrete numeric encodings.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe for initial F1 stop, then request-up workflow F1->MU2->F2 and immediate next request F2->MU3->F3 with hbrg stop/up outputs
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_then_up_to_f2_and_f3

scenario_results.description: default-init probe that dispatches to F1, then PS3 must choose direct upward motion MU3 and S3 must stop at F3
scenario_results.name: default_init_direct_request_to_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe from reachable F2: PS1 must select downward MD1 and S1 arrival must stop at F1
scenario_results.name: hot_start_f2_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe from reachable F3: PS2 must select downward MD2 and S2 arrival must stop at F2
scenario_results.name: hot_start_f3_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe from reachable F3: PS1 must target MD1 rather than MD2, and S1 must stop at F1
scenario_results.name: hot_start_f3_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-reset probe from upward motion MU3; Reset must force F1 stop regardless of outstanding request context
scenario_results.name: reset_from_up_motion_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-reset probe from downward motion MD2; Reset must force F1 stop regardless of outstanding request context
scenario_results.name: reset_from_down_motion_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe from floor F2: no event should leave the stopped floor unchanged, and Reset from a floor must force F1 stop
scenario_results.name: reset_from_floor_and_no_event_stability

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL declares all seven leaf states.
NL specifies F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL includes these transitions exactly.
NL specifies MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL includes these transitions exactly.
NL says hbrg distinguishes upward, downward, and stop; DSL assigns hbrg=1 in MU2/MU3, hbrg=-1 in MD1/MD2, and hbrg=0 in F1/F2/F3.
NL says reset forces floor 1 regardless of context; DSL has forced transition ! * -> F1 :: Reset.
findings.summary: The DSL closely follows the explicit elevator FSM requirements: floor states, motion states, request-triggered movement transitions, arrival-sensor transitions, stop/up/down hbrg assignments, initial F1, and forced Reset to F1 are represented.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions, 7 forced Reset transitions, 7 events, 1 variable, and 7 actions.

GroundingMap includes required elements for all states, request events PS1/PS2/PS3, sensor events S1/S2/S3, Reset, hbrg, hbrg actions, all request transitions, all arrival transitions, initial transition, and forced reset.
sim_summary reports ok=true with 8/8 scenarios passed, including upward paths, downward paths, direct F1-to-F3, reset from motion states, reset from floor state, and no-event floor stability.
findings.summary: Required components are materially covered by the DSL and supported by simulation coverage.

evidence: NL says the controller 'immediately checks the next destination before deciding whether to continue moving' and reset applies 'regardless of the outstanding request context'.
DSL has no request/destination variable and no queue/context state; PS1/PS2/PS3 are modeled only as transition events from floor states.

GroundingMap source_summary assumes PS/S/Reset are discrete events rather than persistent variables because no holding semantics are specified. This is plausible, but it narrows the interpretation of 'outstanding request context'.
findings.summary: The model does not represent persistent queued requests or explicit destination memory, so the phrase about checking the next destination and reset ignoring outstanding request context is implemented only as event-driven re-evaluation after reaching a floor.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary contains advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: Variable 'hbrg' does not affect any transition guard.
NL describes hbrg as an output that distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
DSL uses hbrg in enter actions as an output encoding, which is consistent with the NL.
findings.summary: The W_UNREFERENCED_VAR warning for hbrg should not drive a repair that forces hbrg into guards; hbrg is an output, not a decision variable in the NL.

evidence: All explicitly enumerated required states, transitions, reset behavior, and hbrg output actions are present.
design_diagnostics_summary has blocking_count=0 and only one advisory output-variable warning.
sim_summary passes 8/8 scenarios with targeted tests for major NL paths.
The remaining gap concerns an ambiguity in whether requests are transient events or persistent outstanding context, not a missing explicitly enumerated transition.
findings.summary: No blocking NFRR quality cap is indicated. Estimated tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate, with a minor interpretive caveat around request persistence/destination memory.

evidence: NL explicitly says PS1/PS2/PS3 are floor-request inputs and gives event-like trigger transitions.
NL also mentions 'next destination' and 'outstanding request context', which could imply memory if interpreted more strongly.
GroundingMap source_summary documents the modeling assumption that PS inputs are discrete events rather than persistent variables.
findings.summary: The only quality concern arises from requirement/abstraction ambiguity: the NL mixes event-triggered floor requests with wording that suggests possible outstanding request context, while the DSL and grounding choose a transient-event abstraction.
